rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites profess faith to believers to protect their lives, property, and families, then assure their leaders and fellow polytheists that they remain allies and only mock the believers.
rows.anchor: خداعا عن دمائهم وأموالهم وذراريهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Jewish men told the Prophet’s companions they followed their religion, then told their own leaders they were with them and merely mocking.
rows.anchor: كان رجال من اليهود إذا لقوا أصحاب النبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Their devils were Jews who urged them to deny the Messenger and oppose his teaching; they then claimed to share their companions’ religion.
rows.anchor: شياطينهم من يهود الذين يأمرونهم بالتكذيب

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The hypocrites’ devils are the leading figures in disbelief.
rows.anchor: أما شياطينهم، فهم رءوسهم في الكفر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Their devils are their chiefs and leaders in evil.
rows.anchor: رؤسائهم وقادتهم في الشر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: In another interpretation, their devils are the polytheists.
rows.anchor: قال المشركون

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Their devils are the hypocrites’ companions among the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: أصحابهم من الكفار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Their devils are their companions among hypocrites and polytheists.
rows.anchor: أصحابهم من المنافقين والمشركين

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Their devils are their brothers from among the polytheists.
rows.anchor: إخوانهم من المشركين

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: When believers prospered, hypocrites claimed fellowship with them, but in private they mocked the believers.
rows.anchor: إذا أصاب المؤمنين رخاء، قالوا إنا نحن معكم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The phrase’s devils means the hypocrites’ companions among hypocrites and polytheists.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: " {شياطينهم} [البقرة: 14]

rows.speaker: نحويي البصرة
rows.claim: A Basran grammarian says khala ila means private conversation for a particular need, while khala bihi can mean either private need or mockery; ila avoids ambiguity.
rows.anchor: يقال خلوت إلى فلان، إذا أريد به: خلوت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative analysis takes ila to mean with, since Arabic prepositions can substitute for one another; the cited verse uses ila in the sense of with.
rows.anchor: {من أنصاري إلى الله} [آل عمران: 52] يريد مع الله

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited line uses ʿalayya to mean ʿannī, illustrating substitution among prepositions.
rows.anchor: إذا رضيت علي بنو قشير

rows.speaker: نحويي أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufan analysis takes the phrase as turning their private attention toward their devils; al-Tabari prefers it because ila has its own proper sense and should not be replaced without proof.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول عندي أولى بالصواب، لأن لكل حرف من حروف المعاني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Buying misguidance for guidance means exchanging disbelief for faith.
rows.anchor: أي الكفر بالإيمان

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The hypocrites took misguidance and abandoned guidance.
rows.anchor: أخذوا الضلالة وتركوا الهدى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: They preferred misguidance over guidance.
rows.anchor: استحبوا الضلالة على الهدى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: They had believed and then disbelieved.
rows.anchor: آمنوا ثم كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who say they took misguidance and left guidance treat guidance as the price surrendered for the misguidance acquired.
rows.anchor: الهدى الذي تركاه هو الثمن الذي جعلاه عوضا من الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who read buying as preferring understand the phrase as choosing misguidance over guidance, with ba and ʿala sometimes substituting and ishtara used for choosing.
rows.anchor: أولئك الذين اختاروا الضلالة على الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited al-Aʿsha line uses مشتراة for a woman chosen and brought out of seclusion, supporting the sense of buying as choosing.
rows.anchor: فقد أخرج الكاعب المشتراة من خدرها وأشيع القمارا

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma uses شراة for chosen ones, supporting the interpretation of ishtira as selection.
rows.anchor: وقال ذو الرمة في الاشتراء بمعنى الاختيار

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet likewise calls the choicest property شراة, illustrating choice rather than a literal transaction.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر في مثل ذلك: [البحر السريع] إن الشراة روقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari rejects the choice interpretation because the following statement that their trade did not profit points to an actual exchange of one thing for another.
rows.anchor: فدل بذلك على أن معنى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a literal exchange would fit people who first believed and then disbelieved, the opening description shows these hypocrites never entered Islam; their profession of faith was a lie.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله وباليوم الآخر وما هم بمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purchase wording alone cannot prove prior faith, since buying can mean acquiring something by leaving another thing or choosing it.
rows.anchor: الاشتراء عند مخالفيه قد يكون أخذ شيء بترك آخر غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By trading guidance for misguidance, hypocrites lost: they exchanged clarity and security for confusion, blindness, fear, and terror now, as well as punishment later.
rows.anchor: اختارا الحيرة والعمى على الرشاد والهدى والخوف والرعب على الحفظ والأمن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: They moved from guidance to error, unity to division, security to fear, and Sunnah to innovation.
rows.anchor: خرجوا من الهدى إلى الضلالة، ومن الجماعة إلى الفرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression their trade did not profit means they themselves made no profit; Arabic idiom can attribute an action to its setting and omit what listeners readily supply.
rows.anchor: وإنما معنى ذلك: فما ربحوا في تجارتهم لا فيما اشتروا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A cited poetic line says the worst fate is a man dying among his family, omitting the understood noun death.
rows.anchor: كما قال الشاعر: [البحر الطويل] وشر المنايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of the cited line attributes sleeping to the night while meaning that the person himself slept, illustrating the idiom’s omitted subject.
rows.anchor: حارث قد فرجت عني همي

rows.speaker: جرير بن الخطفي
rows.claim: Jarir attributes blindness and sight to day and night while describing the man, another example of attributing an action to its setting.
rows.anchor: قال جرير بن الخطفي: [البحر الطويل] وأعور من نبهان أما نهاره

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: After God gave the two parables of the hypocrites, they objected that God was too exalted to offer such examples; the passage from the mosquito verse through the losers answered them.
rows.anchor: لما ضرب الله هذين المثلين للمنافقين

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: The mosquito parable depicts worldly life: a mosquito lives while hungry but dies when sated, as worldly people are seized once filled with prosperity.
rows.anchor: قال: هذا مثل ضربه الله للدنيا، إن البعوضة تحيا ما جاعت

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: A variant says that when worldly people’s appointed terms end, they are like a mosquito that dies after drinking its fill, and God suddenly takes them.
rows.anchor: فإذا خلت آجالهم، وانقطعت مدتهم، صاروا كالبعوضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari frames the broken-covenant point through competing definitions, beginning with the general view that the covenant is God’s charge to creation.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هو وصية الله إلى خلقه، وأمره إياهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view takes the covenant as God’s commands and prohibitions delivered through scripture and messengers; breaking it means failing to act on them.
rows.anchor: هو وصية الله إلى خلقه، وأمره إياهم بما أمرهم به من طاعته

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view limits the passage to disbelieving and hypocritical People of the Book: they broke the Torah covenant to follow Muhammad and disclose what they knew about him.
rows.anchor: هو ما أخذه الله عليهم في التوراة من العمل بما فيها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A broader view says all polytheists, disbelievers, and hypocrites break the covenant of monotheism and prophetic proof by rejecting what evidence shows to be true.
rows.anchor: جميع أهل الشرك والكفر والنفاق وعهده إلى جميعهم في توحيده

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view identifies the covenant as the pledge made when God brought Adam’s descendants forth; breaking it means failing to honor that pledge.
rows.anchor: العهد الذي أخذه عليهم حين أخرجهم من صلب آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that the passage initially concerns Jewish scholars in Medina and nearby Israelites, alongside hypocritical polytheists, while applying to everyone who follows their misguidance.
rows.anchor: الآيات نزلت في كفار أحبار اليهود الذين كانوا بين ظهراني مهاجر رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broken covenant is the known duty to affirm Muhammad and reveal his prophethood rather than conceal it, as the Torah pledge required.
rows.anchor: التاركون ما عهد الله إليهم من الإقرار بمحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immediate address is supported by the earlier descriptions of disbelievers and hypocrites and the later special address to the Children of Israel; the warning also reaches all peoples on their path.
rows.anchor: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأوفوا بعهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After God’s confirmed covenant means after He had formally bound them to keep what He required; the word mīthāq is the noun from tawaththuqu, and its pronoun refers to God.
rows.anchor: والميثاق اسم منه، والهاء في الميثاق عائدة على اسم الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning also includes anyone who breaks covenants, cuts ties, and spreads corruption in the same way as the hypocrites and disbelievers.
rows.anchor: كل من كان بالصفة التي وصف الله بها هؤلاء الفاسقين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada warns against breaking the covenant: God hates it and threatens it, and anyone who gives God a sincere pledge must fulfill it.
rows.anchor: فإياكم ونقض هذا الميثاق، فإن الله قد كره نقضه

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: When hypocrites have the upper hand they display six traits, adding covenant-breaking, severing ties, and corruption to lying, broken promises, and betrayal; when weakened they show the first three.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت لهم الظهرة أظهروا هذه الخلال الست جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God commands people to join is kinship: relatives connected through one maternal line; severing it means unjustly withholding their due rights and kindness.
rows.anchor: الذين جمعتهم وإياه رحم والدة واحدة، وقطع ذلك ظلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, the relative expression with yuṣala is governed by the preposition’s implied genitive and refers back to the pronoun in bihi: what God ordered to be joined.
rows.anchor: وأن التي مع يوصل في محل خفض بمعنى ردها على موضع الهاء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the severed ties as kinship and family relations.
rows.anchor: فقطع والله ما أمر الله به أن يوصل بقطيعة الرحم والقرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A broader reading includes severing the Messenger, believers, and their relations; al-Tabari finds it plausible and concludes that every severing of what God ordered joined is condemned.
rows.anchor: فهي دالة على ذم الله كل قاطع قطع ما أمر الله بوصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Losers are those who diminish their own share of God’s mercy through disobedience, like merchants who lose capital; disbelievers and hypocrites lose mercy when they most need it at resurrection.
rows.anchor: الناقصون أنفسهم حظوظها بمعصيتهم الله من رحمته

rows.speaker: جرير بن عطية
rows.claim: Jarir uses khusār for what diminishes people’s share of honor and nobility, illustrating the loss sense.
rows.anchor: قال جرير بن عطية: [البحر الرجز] إن سليطا في الخسار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the losers as the doomed; this can express the same loss of mercy without defining the word itself as doom.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إن معنى {أولئك هم الخاسرون}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Labels such as loser applied to non-Muslims mean unbelief, while such labels applied to Muslims mean sin.
rows.anchor: كل شيء نسبه الله إلى غير أهل الإسلام من اسم مثل خاسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refers to Israelites who heard God’s word and distorted it after understanding; when they met believers they claimed to believe in Muhammad and his revelation, adopting hypocrites’ ways.
rows.anchor: يعني بذلك أنهم إذا لقوا الذين صدقوا بالله وبمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Some Jews told Muhammad they believed, then privately asked one another whether to reveal what God had disclosed to them.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن نفرا من اليهود كانوا إذا لقوا محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم قالوا: آمنا

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Jewish hypocrites said they believed when they met the Prophet’s companions.
rows.anchor: يعني المنافقين من اليهود كانوا إذا لقوا أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قالوا آمنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: They said they believed in the Prophet, but only for the believers’ benefit.
rows.anchor: أي بصاحبكم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولكنه إليكم خاصة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The people in question were Jews who believed and then became hypocrites.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء ناس من اليهود آمنوا ثم نافقوا

none: Bare heading and verse reference only; no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw joins Jacob to Abraham: Jacob also instructed his sons in Islam after Abraham had instructed his sons.
rows.anchor: يقول: ووصى بها يعقوب بنيه بعد إبراهيم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Jacob gave his sons the same testament after Abraham.
rows.anchor: ووصى بها يعقوب بنيه بعد إبراهيم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abraham and Jacob both instructed their sons in Islam.
rows.anchor: وصاهم بالإسلام، ووصى يعقوب بمثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari rejects parsing Abraham’s clause as complete and Jacob’s as a new subject with a different testament; both patriarchs urged obedience, humility, and Islam.
rows.anchor: ولا معنى لقول من قال ذلك؛ ولأن الذي أوصى به يعقوب بنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle an is omitted because a testament is speech in meaning, so the construction follows the verb say; the verse at 4:11 and poetry illustrate this semantic syntax.
rows.anchor: لأن الوصية قول فحملت على معناها

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
rows.claim: Another grammarian says an is omitted because the vocative يا بني suffices, though Arabs sometimes use particles without an and sometimes add it.
rows.anchor: إنما حذفت أن من قوله: {ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه ويعقوب}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose and selected the religion He had already entrusted to Abraham’s descendants; the definite article marks a religion made familiar to them by their ancestors’ testament.
rows.anchor: قد عرفوه بوصيتهما إياهم به ووصيتهما إليهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not die except as Muslims means never leave Islam during life, since no one knows when death will come; otherwise they may die outside God’s chosen faith under His anger and perish.
rows.anchor: أي فلا تفارقوا هذا الدين وهو الإسلام أيام حياتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am kuntum shahada is a fresh question after prior speech, asking whether the Jews and Christians witnessed Jacob’s death; they did not, so must not falsely claim the patriarchs followed their religions.
rows.anchor: أكنتم يا معشر اليهود والنصارى المكذبين بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، الجاحدين نبوته، حضور يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes Jewish and Christian claims about Abraham and Jacob: God sent them and their descendants upon the upright submission to God, which they taught their children.
rows.anchor: ابتعثت خليلي إبراهيم وولده إسحاق وإسماعيل وذريتهم بالحنيفية المسلمة

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: The address asking who witnessed Jacob’s final instruction is directed to the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع: " قوله: {أم كنتم شهداء} [البقرة: 133]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second idh restates the first in apposition: Jacob spoke to his sons when death approached, asking what they would worship after his death.
rows.anchor: يعقوب إذ قال يعقوب لبنيه حين حضور موته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s sons answered that they would worship the one God of Jacob and their forefathers, dedicating worship and lordship to Him alone without associating anything with Him.
rows.anchor: نخلص له العبادة ونوحد له الربوبية فلا نشرك به شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslimun may be a circumstantial description of their worship or a separate statement that they remain submissive afterward; al-Tabari prefers the circumstantial reading.
rows.anchor: وأحسن هذين الوجهين في تأويل ذلك أن يكون بمعنى الحال

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ishmael is listed before Isaac because he was older.
rows.anchor: بدأ بإسماعيل لأنه أكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anomalous reading أبيك is mistaken: Arabic can call an uncle a father, so Ishmael belongs among the forefathers; the canonical reading آبائك is supported by the readers’ consensus, and ilahan is circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: والصواب من القراءة عندنا في ذلك: {وإله آبائك}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being Muslim means submission through obedience and worship; the prophetic response identifies those who affirm all revelation as Muslims.
rows.anchor: لا نفرق بين أحد منهم ونحن له مسلمون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Jews asked which messengers he believed in, Muhammad affirmed all revelation, including Jesus; they rejected Jesus, prompting the response in 5:59.
rows.anchor: فلما ذكر عيسى جحدوا نبوته وقالوا: لا نؤمن بعيسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second version of the report names Nafiʿ ibn Abi Nafiʿ where the first version named Rafiʿ ibn Abi Rafiʿ.
rows.anchor: قال: ونافع بن أبي نافع، مكان رافع بن أبي رافع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The command to affirm all revelation requires believers to believe in every prophet and messenger without distinguishing among them.
rows.anchor: أمر الله المؤمنين أن يؤمنوا ويصدقوا بأنبيائه ورسله كلهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The twelve sons of Jacob each became the ancestor of a people, so they were called the tribes.
rows.anchor: الأسباط: يوسف وإخوته بنو يعقوب، ولد اثني عشر رجلا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi lists Jacob’s sons as Joseph, Benjamin, Reuben, Judah, Simeon, Levi, Dan, and Kohath.
rows.anchor: أما الأسباط فهم بنو يعقوب: يوسف، وبنيامين،

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says Jacob’s twelve sons each fathered a people, forming the tribes.
rows.anchor: الأسباط: يوسف وإخوته بنو يعقوب اثنا عشر رجلا، فولد لكل رجل

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq gives Jacob’s genealogy and wives’ children, concluding that the twelve sons became twelve tribes whose number and lineages only God knows.
rows.anchor: فكان بنو يعقوب اثني عشر رجلا، نشر الله منه اثني عشر سبطا

none: Bare heading and verse reference only; no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari notes that he has already explained the purchase metaphor and the differing interpretations, so he does not repeat that argument here.
rows.anchor: وكذلك بينا وجه: {اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى} [البقرة: 16] باختلاف المختلفين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The phrase means how brazen they are to perform deeds that bring them near the Fire.
rows.anchor: فما أجرأهم على العمل الذي يقربهم إلى النار

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: They have no patience for the Fire; the phrase instead marvels at how daring they are toward it.
rows.anchor: والله ما لهم عليها من صبر، ولكن ما أجرأهم على النار

rows.speaker: مجاهد أو سعيد بن جبير أو بعض أصحابه
rows.claim: The phrase means how brazen they are toward the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد أو سعيد بن جبير، أو بعض أصحابه

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: They are daring and seemingly patient toward the Fire.
rows.anchor: ما أجرأهم وأصبرهم على النار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another interpretation says they are practiced in falsehood and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ما أعملهم بالباطل

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The particle ma is interrogative: what could make them endure the Fire?
rows.anchor: هذا على وجه الاستفهام، يقول: ما الذي أصبرهم على النار

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A question asks what makes them endure the Fire after abandoning truth and following falsehood.
rows.anchor: ما يصبرهم على النار حين تركوا الحق واتبعوا الباطل

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
rows.claim: He reads the clause as a question, arguing that a statement about patience would have a different case ending.
rows.anchor: هذا استفهام، ولو كانت من الصبر قال

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: The question asks what made them persist in the Fire and dare to act as they did.
rows.anchor: ما هذا الذي صبرهم على النار حتى جرأهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد، الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: Another view treats the words as an exclamation at their audacity in doing the deeds of those destined for the Fire.
rows.anchor: فما أشد جرأتهم على النار بعملهم أعمال أهل النار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also explains the phrase as asking how skilled they are at the deeds of the Fire’s people.
rows.anchor: ما أعملهم بأعمال أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the exclamation that they are brazen toward the Fire and expert in its people’s deeds; Arabic uses this construction for audacity, and Fire stands for its punishment.
rows.anchor: وأولى هذه الأقوال بتأويل الآية قول من قال: ما أجرأهم على النار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wonder concerns scholars who concealed Muhammad’s prophethood for bribes despite knowing this would earn God’s anger; mentioning Fire stands for its punishment, as comparisons to Hatim and Antara omit the repeated quality.
rows.anchor: وإنما معنى ذلك: «فما أجرأهم على عذاب النار»

none: Bare heading and verse reference only; no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation links tabarraza to going out onto open land to relieve oneself, just as taghawwata is named after going to low ground.
rows.anchor: كما قيل تغوط لأنهم كانوا يقضون حاجتهم في الغائط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative says the armies gathered, David volunteered against Jalut, combined stones named Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and a stone struck Jalut through the head and routed his forces.
rows.anchor: فكن حجرا واحدا، قال: فأخذهن وأخذ مقلاعا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: After crossing the river, Talut offered half his kingdom to whoever killed Jalut; David left his flock, volunteered despite his brothers’ scorn, and Talut armed him.
rows.anchor: فقال طالوت للناس: لو أن جالوت قتل أعطيت الذي يقتله نصف ملكي

rows.speaker: ابن جريج عن مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid’s report says David took three stones; they spoke of earlier victories, joined together, promised to aid him, and foretold that the stone would kill Jalut with God’s help.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: قال مجاهد: كان بعث أبو داود مع داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadayantum covers deferred sales and purchases, lending, and other debt exchanges due at a known, fixed time; it includes loans, forward sales, and permissible sales with deferred payment.
rows.anchor: يعني إذا تبايعتم بدين أو اشتريتم به، أو تعاطيتم، أو أخذتم به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed specifically about forward purchase of wheat by known measure and due date.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية: {إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه} [البقرة: 282] في السلم في الحنطة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas again identifies the setting as forward purchase of wheat, with its measure and date specified.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى} [البقرة: 282] في السلف في الحنطة

rows.speaker: قتادة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas affirms that a guaranteed forward sale with a specified term is lawful and authorized by God.
rows.anchor: أشهد أن السلف المضمون، إلى أجل مسمى أن الله عز وجل قد أحله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added phrase bidain clarifies the intended legal sense because tadayantum can mean mutual repayment or general giving and taking, not only a debt transaction.
rows.anchor: أبان الله بقوله {بدين} [البقرة: 282] المعنى الذي قصد تعريفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some call bidain mere emphasis, as in 15:30, but al-Tabari says that explanation has no merit here.
rows.anchor: ولا معنى لما قال من ذلك في هذا الموضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari takes write it to mean documenting the debt due at the appointed time, whether from a sale or loan, then introduces a dispute about whether writing is obligatory or recommended.
rows.anchor: ذكر من قال ذلك: حدثني المثنى، قال: ثنا إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported position holds that documentation, though originally obligatory, was later abrogated by the mutual-trust provision.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: كان اكتتاب الكتاب بالدين فرضا، فنسخه قوله:

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Anyone selling for a fixed future date was commanded to document the transaction, whether small or large.
rows.anchor: من باع إلى أجل مسمى أمر أن يكتب صغيرا كان أو كبيرا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: A borrower should write the debt, while a seller should obtain witnesses.
rows.anchor: فمن ادان دينا فليكتب، ومن باع فليشهد

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the writing requirement was initially obligatory.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع، في قوله: " {إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه} [البقرة: 282] فكان هذا واجبا

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: A second report from al-Rabiʿ says the trust provision in the next verse granted a concession.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع، بمثله، وزاد فيه: قال: ثم قامت الرخصة والسعة

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان المرعشي
rows.claim: A seller who failed to document or witness a debt and was later denied it had sinned, so his prayer against the debtor would not be answered.
rows.anchor: رجل باع شيئا فلم يكتب ولم يشهد، فلما حل ماله

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Another view treats the writing rule as relaxed when parties trust one another, allowing them not to document or witness the transaction under the next verse.
rows.anchor: لا بأس إذا أمنته أن لا تكتب، ولا تشهد

rows.speaker: عامر
rows.claim: The trust provision grants permission for anyone who chooses to entrust the other party without documentation.
rows.anchor: رخص في ذلك، فمن شاء أن يأتمن صاحبه فليأتمنه
